text: AI coding agents have made individual developers dramatically more productive, yet most organizations aren't seeing anything close to that gain at the company level.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: A key reason is that shipping a feature to production involves far more than writing code.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Triage, review, context, guardrails, and human approvals all surround the work, and agents add new risk by acting in ways teams can't always see or control.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Turning individual gains into real organizational throughput has become one of the central challenges of the agentic era.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Port is an AI software factory platform that lets platform engineers build, operate, and govern an AI software factory, which is a layer that sits above the coding agents.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: The factory is model and agent agnostic, while supplying a context lake that encodes an organization's taxonomy and data, governance, and guardrails across each stage of the software lifecycle.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Human-in-the-loop checkpoints, orchestration across different agents, and a registry of approved agents and skills.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: Yonatan Boguslavsky is the CTO and a co-founder at Port.
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: In this episode, he joins Kevin Ball to talk about the shift from writing features to factory engineering, how a context lake structures organizational knowledge so agents can actually use it, how governance works across an agentic software lifecycle,
speaker: SPEAKER_01

text: And the build versus buy question of where a platform like Port fits.
